name: ORBIT 2.0
teaser: Bots play the raid like you do, and a "Ghost Mode" to run it all at high fps
description:
⚠️ Heads up: ORBIT is built on Phobos’s foundation (MIT-licensed, with Janky’s blessing). Full credits at the bottom 🙏

ORBIT - Objective-driven Raid Bot Intelligence Tactics

Smarter bots. Real objectives. Raids that feel alive.

Every bot squad in your raid follows a plan: a rich area to strip, a PvP hotspot to hunt, a quest spot to visit. They work it as a team, loot like players, upgrade their gear along the way, and head for extract when they’re done. Kill one late in the raid and his backpack tells the story of where he’s been.

👻 Ghost Mode: far-away bots go dormant to free your CPU while the raid keeps progressing. My heavy-population benchmark measured +45% average fps, with testers reporting +50 to +100% depending on their setup.

New in 2.1: Ghost movement for supported vanilla and faction bots, zones by floor and bot type, presets and addon support, expanded Ghost hearing settings, and an option to wake bots for spectating. Configure it all through the server web UI and visual Zone Editor.

📷 Screenshot

Pair it with the latest Raid Review to replay it all on the post-raid map.

Questions, bug reports, feedback: ORBIT Discord thread.

What A Raid Looks Like
  • A 4-man squad rolls “clean out Resort”, splits the rooms, opens a locked door or two, and extracts once the bags are worth it.
  • The squad’s Rat grabs the 5k mag his Chad walked past: personalities decide everything.
  • Scavs hold their turf; a lucky few roam the whole map.
  • Gunfire behind a hill: two ghost squads settling it off-screen. Push the sound and the fight turns real.
The Pillars

🎯 Objectives and extraction

ORBIT-controlled PMC and PlayerScav squads roll 1-5 goals at spawn: high-value loot zones, kill hunts anchored on PvP hotspots, real EFT quest triggers. The leader takes the anchor, the others splinter to nearby loot and cover. They extract for real reasons - enough roubles, goals completed, or the raid clock - and they coordinate on shared exfils like the car.

🎒 Looting that feels human

ORBIT-controlled bots use a custom loot engine built on B**’s own pickup APIs. Per-personality value thresholds (a GigaChad ignores what a Rat treasures), realistic search timings and animations, inside-out container draining, and mid-raid gear upgrades: a bot that finds a better rifle swaps to it, strips the good mods off his old one, and leaves it on the corpse for you to find. Money, fragmentation grenades and dogtags bypass value checks when the bot has room; secured containers are never touched. Coverage rolls make squads miss a few items per room, like real players do.

Bots can collect nearby valuables before leaving after reaching their loot threshold, so one expensive marked-room find does not immediately end the looting session. They also remember multiple bodies to loot after consecutive kills.

🧠 Personalities run the show

ORBIT uses SAIN personalities to shape PMC behaviour: what’s worth picking up, how much of a room gets covered, who hunts and who rats, how early they extract, whether they force locked doors, even how strong a ghost squad fights off-screen. Two squads never play the same raid.

🗺️ Your raid, your rules

Every behaviour setting lives in a web UI on your SPT server (/orbit, one button away from the F12 menu), including headless setups. Most settings apply next raid; faction takeover and personality brain list changes require a game restart.

Presets keep settings and zones together: save your own setups, switch between addons, or export a complete preset to share. Editing Default or an addon creates a personal Custom copy. Your existing 2.0 settings and zones migrate automatically.

Addon presets are detected automatically. A zones-only addon preserves your behaviour settings, and updates to the selected addon are picked up automatically. Personal copies keep their own tuning.

👻 Ghost Mode

Distant bots keep progressing while their expensive full AI sleeps. Ghost Mode ships ON by default and can be disabled in the web UI.

ORBIT-controlled Ghost squads keep walking their routes and looting in real time. When hostile Ghost groups meet, their fight can be simulated with audible gunfire matching their actual weapons, including suppressors, real casualties and lootable corpses. Get close during the encounter and it becomes a real firefight.

Bots can wake through proximity, damage or scoped observation. Sleep distances, eligible bot types, movement, looting and fight settings are configurable.

Vanilla and faction bots

Supported vanilla bots and factions can now move in Ghost Mode while keeping their own patrols, hunts, checkpoint orders and regrouping logic. ORBIT does not need to take over their behaviour.

  • Enable their Dormant toggle, Ghost movement and Vanilla / faction movement.
  • Leave faction Take over toggles OFF, or keep Vanilla behaviour enabled for the relevant bot type, to preserve that routing.
  • Raiders and Rogues have separate controls.

Native pauses and guard duties still apply. Unsupported actions, combat and some physical interactions may require a bot to wake. Bots keeping their original routing are not influenced by ORBIT’s zones.

Hearing

Eligible Ghosts can hear gunfire and decide whether to investigate. Set investigation chances by PMC personality or bot category, with separate hearing ranges for PMC/PlayerScavs, other vanilla bots and added factions. Unsuppressed and suppressed ranges, minimum shot count, cooldown and combat grouping are configurable in collapsible panels. Sniper Scavs and UNTAR/RUAF checkpoint guards do not investigate gunfire through this system.

Spectating

Enable Wake bots for spectating to wake the remaining bots and pause Ghost Mode once the last human player dies or extracts.

Using Fika? See the Fika tab for installation and the sound-sync addon.

🗺️ Zone Editor

Draw the hotspots that steer squad routing, straight on a real render of each map: drag, resize, attract or repel, tune the game’s own zones, mark kill-hunt anchors, preview the pull with live arrows, set per-map player convergence.

New in 2.1: name custom zones, assign them to specific floors and bot types or factions, and switch between floor plans. Matching zones are highlighted, and highlighted zones take priority when selecting overlapping areas.

How zones work: they never override the AI, they tilt it. Every time a squad picks its next destination it blends several pulls (its momentum, its main objective, some randomness, and every zone’s force within reach), so a strong positive Force makes an area win those rolls way more often, a negative Force pushes squads away, and Radius is how far the influence reaches. Once they arrive, the normal behaviour (looting, guarding, questing, fighting) takes over. You can’t hard-force “8 PMCs go to Dorms”, but a big Force on Dorms means most squads passing nearby will swing through sooner or later.

Zones influence ORBIT-controlled bots, awake or Ghost. Bots keeping their native or faction routing without takeover follow their own logic. Destinations still need a reachable path on the chosen floor; zones do not create routes or operate switches.

Export your setup as a zone pack, or include it in a complete preset with your behaviour settings. Try the community packs in the Recommended Addons tab. Map renders courtesy of tarkov.dev.

Recommended Addons

I recommend Baseline Zones by FoxHead to expand ORBIT’s default zones and give bots more places to visit. It’s a zones-only addon, so it keeps your behaviour settings.

Also try Live-Like ORBIT by TomiNyxer, which combines behaviour settings and zones for a different raid experience.

The two feel quite different, so try a few raids with each and see which you prefer!

Try both with the preset system (coming in 2.1):

  1. Install both addons using their ORBIT 2.1 versions (once available) and follow their installation instructions.
  2. Save your current setup with Presets > Save as new preset.
  3. Choose either addon from the Preset selector at the top of the web UI before your next raid.

To try ORBIT defaults + Baseline, select Default first, then Baseline. Since Baseline only supplies zones, selecting it directly after Live-Like would keep Live-Like’s behaviour settings.

Restart the game if your preset changes faction takeover or personality brain lists. Raid Review is useful for comparing where bots go and what they do.

Install & Setup
  1. Install the dependencies: BigBrain · Waypoints · SAIN
  2. Extract the zip into your SPT root folder (client plugin + server mod).
  3. Configure from the web UI: F12 → Open web config UI (or browse to https://127.0.0.1:6969/orbit).

Upgrading from 2.0: close the game and server, then extract over your existing ORBIT installation. Keep your settings and zones; 2.1 migrates them automatically.

Fika users: follow the Fika tab and install on every machine.

Recommended SAIN setup (2 tweaks)

1. Personality spread - ORBIT was tuned around this distribution. SAIN’s config is a web UI too since 4.1: browse to https://127.0.0.1:6969/sain/presets (your server address), open the Personalities tab, and for each personality below set Can Be Randomly Assigned = On with its Randomly Assigned Chance:

Personality Chance
Rat 10
Wreckless 5
SnappingTurtle 5
Coward 5
Chad 5
Timmy 3
GigaChad 3

(Heads up for Twitch Player users: it zeroes several of these by default.)

2. Extract layer - let ORBIT own extraction. Same UI, Global Settings → General → Extract: turn SAIN Extract Behavior Off, then Save (editing a built-in preset creates an editable copy).

Fika

Install ORBIT on ALL machines: the SPT server, the headless client if you use one, and every player’s PC.

  1. Follow Install & Setup for the dependencies.
  2. Extract the complete ORBIT ZIP into the SPT root folder on every machine. Keep the same ORBIT version everywhere.
  3. Download the separate ORBIT Fika addon and extract its ZIP there on every machine too.

No need to separate client and server files. Server files simply stay unused on machines that aren’t running the SPT server.

The Fika addon synchronises Ghost battle sounds so every player can hear them, including when bots run on a headless client.

Settings are shared through the SPT server. Use F12 > Open web config UI, or open https://YOUR_SERVER_IP:6969/orbit with your server’s address and port.

Compatibility

Required: SAIN - ORBIT plugs into its personality system.

Recommended: spawn and loadout mods shape who spawns with what gear; ORBIT decides where they go and what they do. The layers don’t fight. APBS, ABPS, Raid Review.

Do not combine with: Questing Bots, Looting Bots, Phobos, or other AI limiter / culling mods such as AILimit and Adaptive Bot Culling. They overlap with systems ORBIT controls.

Faction mods: supported vanilla and faction behaviours can run in Ghost Mode with takeover disabled. Use the per-faction controls to choose who handles routing. Other custom brains may need additional compatibility support.

Troubleshooting

Bots frozen or acting weird? In order:

  1. Check for the unsupported mods above.
  2. Test with vanilla raid times (extended raids are a known trouble source).
  3. If you run ABPS, try regenerating its config from defaults.
  4. Still broken: the 50/50 method.

Before reporting, please reproduce with just ORBIT + SAIN + BigBrain + Waypoints + ABPS on default configs (per Shynd’s classic advice: everyone’s modpack is unique, shrink yours first). Then drop by the ORBIT thread or the SPT support channel.

Roadmap & Known Issues

Delivered in 2.1: Ghost movement for supported vanilla and faction bots, zones by floor and bot type, named custom zones, presets and addon updates, expanded Ghost hearing controls, separate Raider/Rogue settings and waking bots for spectating.

On the list (no ETA, no promises): camp & ambush decisions, post-combat self-heal, squad splitting with radio comms, boss hunting and faction rivalries (Firefly’s idea), airdrop ambushes, a rally-flare item, multi-step objectives (Kiba alarm, ULTRA power, Reserve D-2…), switch-gated and Red-Rebel-style extracts, cross-raid player heatmaps feeding bot routing (Fiodor’s idea), and per-map ORBIT/Ghost settings. Suggestions land on the Discord thread.

Known limits

  • Native Ghost movement supports specific behaviours. Some actions require waking, and other custom brains may need additional support.
  • Most Reserve extracts need switches ORBIT cannot operate yet.
  • If faction takeover causes problems, leave it OFF to preserve the faction’s original routing with supported native Ghost movement.
  • Labs security gates and difficult navigation can still trap bots. Recovery does not resolve every stuck case.
